summary: All 300+ examples pass. There are no errors, no blocking open questions and no blocker-level dev questions. The package is buildable. Five major dev-refinement questions, five non-blocking open questions, several partly unbacked claims and some internal rule ids in the prose need a product owner decision or cleanup. The tariff logic rests on inferred per-child rows, which D-009 makes a go-live verification gate.

findings.title: Insurance start rule: contract start vs actual first working day
findings.why: If the contract starts on the 1st but the first working day is later (weekend or holiday), the rule moves insurance start to the next month. This gives wrong fund registrations. The fund's link between start date and first working day is also unknown.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (feature.md, major); coverage: F-pension_portal-3a97ab unused; US-03.2
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml whether the rule uses the contractual start date or the actual first working day. Confirm with the fund how mid-month starts are handled.

findings.title: Child per-child result is inferred and internally inconsistent
findings.why: Lonio now computes the tariff itself. The rule expression disagrees with its table in at least two cases, and many rows rest only on D-009, which is a verification decision and not a source. Wrong tariff codes are possible.
findings.evidence: trace_judge rule.child_result; inferred_items; OQ-calculator-coverage; US-07.3 to 07.6
findings.action: Have the domain expert reconcile the expression and the table. Run the inferred rows against the Zurich calculator before go-live, as D-009 requires. Keep this as an explicit release gate.

findings.title: Liechtenstein question order and the reservation under the double taxation agreement
findings.why: Liechtenstein residents who return daily get no tariff code, yet they are still asked about denomination, spouse employment and children. This breaks data minimisation. The 'subject to double taxation agreement' reservation for more than 45 non-return days is not recorded in AC-08.4.3.
findings.action: Decide whether the Liechtenstein questions come first or answers are discarded. Decide whether the reservation is recorded and flagged for HR.

findings.title: Residence country timing
findings.why: The home-address country decides source-tax liability, the canton and the cross-border questions. Movers' current address may differ from the one that applies from the first working day.
findings.action: Decide whether to ask for the address applying at the first working day. Add this to the story.

findings.title: House number required without a source
findings.why: Employees whose address has no house number could not submit.
findings.action: Decide whether the house number is optional or allows an explicit 'no house number'.

findings.title: Fund registration gaps (canton abroad, partnership and separated mapping, divorced and widowed)
findings.why: The fund's canton field is required, but employees abroad have no valid value. The Married mapping for registered partners and separated employees is provisional. Divorced and widowed screens are unseen. Registration could be blocked.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton-abroad; OQ-civil-status-partnership; OQ-spouse-dob-other-status; fact_judge F-pension_portal-b359c3, 6d3630, 39bab1; trace_judge rule.pension_fund_civil_status (Separated not backed)
findings.action: Get the fund's answers and a screenshot for Divorced and Widowed. Record the decisions in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Source tax liability rule is hedged by HR
findings.why: Anna said 'I think so' and added conditions over time. 'Here' is read as Switzerland. This rule gates all the source tax questions.
findings.evidence: OQ-source-tax-rule-confirmation; fact_judge F-hr_transcript-550840 and 5af8d0; trace_judge AC-08.3.1
findings.action: Have HR confirm the decision table in writing, including 'lives here' = Switzerland and that everyone living abroad is subject.

findings.title: Stories include behaviour that no cited fact backs
findings.why: Several claims are untraceable. Examples: the confession, children and spouse-works questions; the fixed step order; the Liechtenstein base-letter handling; the 'no maximum number of children' statement; and the date format and permit reminder purposes. Some cite facts that are not in the cited set.
findings.evidence: trace_judge story.US-01.1, US-01.2, US-01.4, US-03.1, US-06.5, US-07.2; rule.questionnaire_flow, cross_border_tariff, liechtenstein_no_source_tax
findings.action: Fix the citations where facts exist. Otherwise mark these items inferred or add decisions. Decide the maximum number of children.

findings.title: Internal rule ids written into business prose
findings.why: Snake_case rule ids and 'expression' wording appear in the feature, stories and open-questions files. This is a minor technical leak.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: feature.md, US-02.3, US-06.4, US-06.5, US-07.1, open-questions.md
findings.action: Replace the ids with business terms such as 'source tax liability rule' and 'per-child result'.

findings.title: Untestable and ambiguous acceptance criteria wording
findings.why: Some wording cannot be tested as written. AC-03.1.2 is untestable. 'Required' and 'asked' are used inconsistently in the example tables. The permit reminder text is missing. The date on which a child's age is judged is not set.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement info: US-03.1, US-05.1, US-05.2, US-01.4, US-07.2
findings.action: Agree the question wording and the permit reminder text with HR. Standardise 'required' in the examples. Fix the child age reference date.
